To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the extracts of custard apple (Anonna squamosa) leaves, seeds and seeds oil were found effective in controlling tobacco cut worm, S. litura in groundnut crop.
custard apple extracts were effective against tobacco cut worm in groundnut and the seed oil based formulation was the most effective.
annona oil based formulations were more effective than aqueous extract in controlling S. litura in groundnut crop.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an effective, safe, eco-friendly, and low cost biopesticide from custard apple plant for the management of S. litura on groundnut crop.
the development of an effective, safe, eco-friendly and cost-effective formulation of custard apple seed oil and leaves for the management of S. litura on groundnut.
the development of a new botanical insecticide from the custard apple (Anona squamosa Linn.) and the results obtained are encouraging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the custard apple leaf extract is a potential biopesticide for the management of Spodoptera liturain Rabi groundnuts.
custard apple seed oil based formulation was found to be the most effective and economical in the management of S. litura on Ragi groundnut.
custard apple is an effective and promising biopesticide for the management of tobacco cut worm on groundnut crop.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the annona oil based formulations can be used for control of Spodoptera liturna on groundnut crop.
custard apple seed oil is the best among all the extracts and custard apple fresh leaf aqueous is the least effective.
custard apple extracts are potential insecticides for groundnut crop.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the custard apple seed oil and leaf extracts could be used as an alternative for the synthetic pesticide in the management of S. litura on groundnut.
custard apple extracts can be used for pest management in groundnut crop.
custard apple is a potential source of bioinsecticide and the farmers can prepare and use the same for their own benefit.
